summary: Stephen H. West is a sinologist who studied at National Taiwan Normal University and the University of Michigan (Ph.D. 1968–1972). He served as executive director of the IUP and held professorships in Chinese at UC Berkeley (~1986–2004) and Arizona State University (~2004).

Stephen J. Laumakis works in philosophy and Buddhist studies. He studied under John Kronen, Ramdas Lamb, George J. Tanabe, and David West, and served as Professor of Philosophy and Director of the Aquinas Scholars Honors Program at the University of St. Thomas (attested 2013).

Stephen Jenkins specializes in religious studies, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology. He studied at Harvard University under doctoral supervisors Masatoshi Nagatomi and Charles Hallisey, alongside several other teachers, and was attested as Professor of Religious Studies at California State Polytechnic University, Humboldt (2010–2013).

Stephen Prothero is a religious studies scholar who earned his B.A. from Yale University (~1978–1982) and his M.A. and Ph.D. from Harvard University (~1984–1990) under William R. Hutchison. Around 1996, he joined Boston University, where he became Professor Emeritus.

Stephen R. Bokenkamp is a scholar of sinology and religious studies who studied at UC Berkeley (~1978–1986). He taught Classical Chinese at Indiana University (~1986–2007) and later served as Professor of Chinese in Religious Studies at Arizona State University (~2007).
Stephen Suen is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned his PhD at The University of Hong Kong (attested 2009) under the doctoral supervision of K. L. Dhammajoti.

Stephen Wootton Bushell (1844–1908) worked in sinology and archaeology. He studied at the University of London, earning an MD (~1866–1868), and held posts as house surgeon at Guy's Hospital (1866) and resident medical officer at Bethlem Royal Hospital (1867).

Steve Odin works in philosophy, religious studies, and Japanology. He completed graduate studies and a postdoc at Stony Brook University under David A. Dilworth and Edward S. Casey, and became Professor of Philosophy at the University of Hawaiʻi in 1982.

Steven Collins (1950–2018) was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He earned his D.Phil. at Oxford under Richard Gombrich and held posts at Bristol (~1980–1991) and the University of Chicago (from 1991) as Chester D. Tripp Professor.

Steven Heine is a religious and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Pennsylvania and Temple University. He held posts at Villanova, La Salle, and Penn State, before becoming a professor at Florida International University in 1997.

Steven Lindquist is an Indology and religious studies scholar who earned his Ph.D. at the University of Texas at Austin under Patrick Olivelle. He also studied under traditional teachers and holds a post at Concordia University.

Steven Lukes is a philosopher and sociologist who studied at Oxford under E. E. Evans-Pritchard. He held posts at Balliol College (1966–1987), European University Institute, University of Florence, University of Siena, LSE, and New York University (~2001–2021).

Steven Neal Weinberger is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology who earned his BA at Amherst and his MA and PhD (2003) at the University of Virginia under Jeffrey Hopkins, later holding an attested post there in 2006.
Stewart McFarlane is a scholar in religious studies, sinology, and Buddhist studies who held an attested post at Lancaster University's Department of Religious Studies in 1991 and 2001.

Sthaneshwar Timalsina is an Indologist and philosopher who studied at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University and Martin Luther University of Halle-Wittenberg. He held posts at Nepal Sanskrit University (~1993–2001), San Diego State University (~2005–2022), and Stony Brook University (~2022).

Stig Wikander (1908–1983) was a Swedish scholar of Indology, Iranian-Central Asian studies, and religion. Educated at Uppsala under Henrik Samuel Nyberg, he taught at Lund (1941–1953) and held the Chair of Sanskrit at Uppsala University (1953–1974).

Stuart H. Blackburn works in Indology. He studied at Wesleyan University (~1961–1965) and the University of California, Berkeley (~1974–1980), and held an academic post at SOAS University of London from ~1995 to 2011.

Stuart Piggott (1910–1996) was an archaeologist and Indologist. He earned a graduate diploma at University College London and the UCL Institute of Archaeology (~1934–1936) studying under Mortimer Wheeler, later holding a post at the University of Edinburgh (~1946–1977).

Stuart Ray Sarbacker is a scholar of religious studies, Indology, and philosophy. He earned his Doctor of Philosophy from the University of Wisconsin-Madison in 2001 under the doctoral supervision of David M. Knipe.

Su Bai (1922–2018) was a Chinese archaeologist, sinologist, and Buddhist studies scholar. He completed graduate studies at Peking University (1940–1944) under teachers including Yongtong Tang and Rong Geng, and served as a professor at Peking University from 1948 to 2004.
